reviewContext.issueReference: none (inline workflowInput.requestedOutcome; opus-terra-design-and-implement-review-loop-session-559, plan review comm-010594, design accepted comm-010590)
reviewContext.userProblem: The Riela session store <session-root>/runtime-records/runtime-message-log.sqlite grows to many GiB (measured: 4.68 GB user store with 768 sessions on 0.2.85; 13 GB events-serve project store; 5.8 GB profile store). Legacy inline session_json and cli_workflow_sessions.record_json duplicate the full session JSON (1.9 GB each), nested child_terminal_json is 488 MB, executions[].inputSnapshot is about 93% of session bytes and re-embeds upstream outputs every loop iteration (848 distinct digests of 862 canonical payload rows), and retention defaults are 'no cap', so riela gc and the automatic run-end pass delete nothing without a retention config. Legacy rows are only converted by a manual riela storage compact --apply.
requiredOutcomes: (A) New execution payloads store each inputSnapshot subtree of >=1024 bytes once per root session as a content-addressed fragment (workflow_runtime_payload_refs, schema generation 12); readers expand and verify digests and fail closed; a synthetic loop benchmark shows baseline >= 5x stored and every public read path (session status/export/logs/progress, GraphQL/web session views, resume/rerun inputs) is byte-identical to the legacy form.

(B1) With no retention config, RielaRetentionPolicy.builtInDefault applies: results 30 days, messages follow results, logs 30 days, no byte cap, automatic true; config, CLI overrides, keepForever and RIELA_RETENTION_AUTOMATIC=0 still win; riela gc --dry-run reports the defaults with policySource default instead of 'no cap'; the generated sweep never runs on a defaulted policy.

(B2) RunEndStorageMaintenance becomes the single automatic maintenance pass (runEnd and scheduled profiles): bounded, resumable, terminal-only, lock-gated conversion of legacy inline snapshots, legacy CLI copies and embedded nested payloads via the existing converters with a storage-maintenance.json cursor (busy retry, park after 3 failures, retired skip), plus bounded incremental vacuum; it runs at workflow run/session resume|rerun|continue end, in events serve and serve via RielaAutomaticStoragePass.runScheduled, and in RielaApp.

(B3) riela doctor storage reports reclaimable.remainingBytes (upper bound), reclaimable.recovery for auto_vacuum=NONE session/definitions stores, and session.maintenance parked-row visibility while staying strictly read-only.
Docs (docs/storage-doctor-and-compact.md, README Runtime Data Retention section, docs/terminal-retention.md) describe the representation, defaults, automatic maintenance and overrides.
swift build succeeds and the retention, gc, storage compact/doctor, run-end maintenance, session store and events serve suites pass.
nonGoals: No payload compression (zlib/zstd) and no Package.swift or Packages/RielaMemory change (design §3.7).
No bulk rewrite of existing generation-11 canonical execution rows.
No new manual commands; no change to riela storage compact behavior or to retention deletion rules, planners, protections, locks or tombstones.
No GraphQL, SDL, SurfaceCatalog or web change.
No edits to Sources/RielaCLI/RielaCLIApplication.swift, Package.swift, Sources/RielaCLI/EventLiveServe.swift or Sources/RielaCLI/ServeHTTPCommand.swift.
No default byte caps; no full VACUUM; no conversion of auto_vacuum=NONE databases.
No version bump, release or push (gitPush=false).
constraints: Backward compatible reads of every on-disk form (legacy inline, legacy CLI copies, embedded nested, generation-11 canonical, new reduced); additive generation-12 DDL only; conversions batch-limited and resumable.
Never delete or rewrite running, paused, waiting or otherwise resumable sessions or retained tree members; never take a held execution lock blockingly or break one.
Default retention only removes fully terminal (completed|failed|cancelled) unprotected families.
Never unlink live SQLite DB/WAL/SHM files; reclamation uses incremental_vacuum plus PASSIVE checkpoint only.
Works on macOS and Linux builds without new dependencies; digests are sha256 of the stored canonical JSON and verified on read.
Tests use realpath-resolved temporary stores, temp HOME and injected clocks; never ~/.riela or a real project store.
A concurrent workflow edits main for YouTube processing; keep changes inside storage/retention/maintenance code and the stated doc sections.

Workers run swift build/test/swiftlint from an arm64 shell (arch -arm64 /bin/zsh -lc), log under tmp/session-storage-gc/<planId>/ (per-attempt subdirectories allowed) with exit status, follow the sha256 pre/post edit drift protocol, never run state-changing git, and write only their own impl-plans/progress/<planId>.md.

Build cache: .build/ and .swiftpm/ are the pre-existing gitignored shared SwiftPM cache; writes by swift build/test/swiftlint are authorized and untracked, are not part of any writePaths/sharedPaths/artifactRoots, must never block a worker or be deleted, and a locked build folder means wait and retry; artifactRoots is intentionally empty for every plan.

Serial reconciliation (not owned by any plan): full-target build, swiftlint over all touched files, fixing out-of-plan tests that hard-code generation 11 or 'no config means no deletion', and archiving the index and plans.
designDecisionsAndRationale: Structural fragment dedup of inputSnapshot instead of compression: the CHECK(json_valid(bytes, 8)) constraint and many SQL json_extract readers make compressed bytes require a table rebuild or a parallel column, and per-payload deflate cannot see the cross-payload repetition that dominates real data (design §3.7).
Only execution payloads are reduced; top-level stepId/status/importedFrom are never hoisted, so SQL json_extract readers stay unchanged.
An escape rule returns the unreduced text when inputSnapshot already contains $rielaPayloadRef, so any stored form decodes unambiguously.
Generation 12 is additive; older binaries refuse the store via the existing newer-generation error because they cannot expand references.

effectivePolicy(for:) fills each absent category with the built-in default while policy(for:) keeps meaning 'configured', so existing callers keep their semantics; messages stay 'follow results' to avoid independent messages-only pruning with tombstones.

Automatic maintenance reuses the existing idempotent converters, SessionExecutionLockRegistry, RetentionTargetLock and RetentionRunStamp-style atomic state instead of adding a parallel mechanism; selection is keyset-on-primary-key with the legacy predicate in the same query.

Scheduler hosts (events serve, serve) already call AutomaticRetentionHook.runAutomaticPass, so extending it via RielaAutomaticStoragePass.runScheduled covers them without editing EventLiveServe.swift or ServeHTTPCommand.swift; RielaApp switches only in EntryPoint+Retention.swift.
riela doctor storage stays read-only: the cursor reader never creates files or directories and no lock is taken.
intentionalTradeoffs: Existing generation-11 canonical rows are not rewritten; only new writes and legacy conversions produce the reduced form.
Upgrade behavior change: stores without config start removing terminal families and logs older than 30 days on the first automatic pass (documented in README and the retention doc).
auto_vacuum=NONE stores only reuse freed pages; doctor reports the required free space and the manual recovery path instead of an automatic full VACUUM.
Per-pass budgets (runEnd 16/256/2 s with retry share 8/128/1 s, vacuum 4096 pages; scheduled 64/1024/10 s with retry share 32/512/5 s, vacuum 65536 pages) defer remaining conversion to later passes.
remainingBytes is a deliberately simple upper bound that may double count.
Only the synthetic >=5x benchmark is gated; the real-store dedup ratio is not measured.
supportedEdgeCases: Legacy inline snapshots, legacy CLI full copies, embedded nested payloads, generation-11 and reduced payloads all load equal.
Missing or corrupted fragment rows make load throw 'runtime payload fragment missing or corrupt'.
Fragments shared across executions and nested invocations are released only when no parent still references them.
keepWorkflowIds without limits keeps the default age plus the kept ids; per-category keepForever; automatic false; RIELA_RETENTION_AUTOMATIC=0 with no config.

Sessions whose execution lock is held go to busy (cap 256, otherwise rescanNeeded) and convert on a later pass; non-terminal rows are skipped permanently; retired rows are skipped; deterministic failures park after 3 attempts with exactly one warning.
Corrupt or missing storage-maintenance.json cursor restarts the scan; automatic.lock held means the pass is skipped.
session resume|rerun|continue store selection honors --scope user and an explicit --session-store.
Doctor on a store without a cursor reports maintenance null and creates nothing.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Shrinking auto_vacuum=NONE databases during automatic passes.
Automatic discovery of stores other than user, project and explicit (--session-store / RIELA_SESSION_STORE).
Downgrade of generation-12 stores to older binaries.
Memory, definitions, KV and cache databases (no reduction and no doctor recovery block for memory/cache/KV).
Pending user confirmation of QA Q1/Q2 default values and Q7 parking behavior (assumed defaults are implemented).
reviewContext.reviewDecision: Step 3 design accepted (comm-010590). Step 5 impl-plan review accepted all 5 plans plus the index (comm-010594): SGC-PLAN-F1 (mid, build-cache/artifactRoots authorization) resolved; residual low items SGC-PLAN-L1 (index wording 'sgc-01 runs alongside W1 and W2' vs wave table; dispatch follows dependsOn, sgc-01 has none), SGC-PLAN-L2 (package-wide build/test while sibling plans edit; mitigated by retry, hash-drift and reconciliation rules), SGC-PLAN-L3 (built-in defaults make no-config gc/compact/hook tests destructive; keep temp HOME and --scope user or temp --working-dir/--session-store isolation).
residualRisks: Q1/Q2 defaults (30-day results and logs, no byte cap) and Q7 parking await user confirmation.
Real-store dedup ratio is not measured; only the synthetic >=5x benchmark is gated.
